correctness.rationale: For each full-support normal u the Fourier transform of the complete parallel-section function is the box volume times the product sinc(s|u_i|a_i/2). The nonzero even coefficients of log sinc and Newton identities uniquely recover the multiset of positive weighted widths. A three-cycle switch preserves the width multisets in both views and total volume, for any two full-support views and every finite d≥3. In generic dimension 3 a nontrivial transposition violates the weighted first sum when ratios r_i differ; eliminating a variable for the two three-cycles gives the checked product factorization, leaving one positive one-dimensional exceptional two-to-one family. Three stated oblique normals have squared-coordinate moment matrix determinant 1/12 and recover all positive side lengths. Independent symbolic factorization and matrix inversion pass.
